codebase_map.architecture_summary: FORGE is a Python-based LLM orchestration framework for automated code remediation. It follows a pipeline pattern: Discovery -> Triage -> Remediation -> Validation. The main entry points are a CLI (typer-based) and an AgentField agent. The execution engine uses checkpointing for resume capability, git worktrees for isolated fixes, and multiple specialized LLM agents for different roles. Configuration is partially centralized in ForgeConfig (Pydantic model) but scattered with magic numbers elsewhere. The codebase has a monolithic app.py orchestrator that needs decomposition. Tests include golden codebases with intentional vulnerabilities for detection testing.
key_patterns: Pipeline pattern with 4 phases: Discovery, Triage, Remediation, Validation
Git worktree isolation for concurrent fix application
Conditional AgentField import with fallback to standalone mode
Pydantic models for schema validation throughout
Token budget management for LLM context windows

findings.title: Command Injection via Unsanitized repo_url in Git Clone
findings.description: In forge/app.py, the _resolve_repo_path function passes the user-supplied repo_url directly to subprocess.run for git clone without validating the URL scheme, format, or content. While shell=False prevents direct shell injection, git itself can interpret certain URL formats (e.g., git://host/repo, file:///etc/passwd, ext::command) in dangerous ways. The workspace name derived from the URL via regex is also used unsanitized as a directory path component. Multiple workers flagged this with high agreement.

locations.snippet:
match = re.search(r"/([^/]+?)(?:\.git)?$", repo_url.rstrip("/"))
name = match.group(1) if match else "repo"
workspace = os.path.join(WORKSPACES_DIR, name)
...
subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "--depth=1", repo_url, workspace], check=True, ...)

findings.suggested_fix: 1) Validate repo_url with urlparse: only allow https:// scheme. 2) Validate hostname against an allowlist or at minimum reject file://, git://, ext::, and other dangerous schemes. 3) Sanitize the extracted repo name to only allow alphanumeric, hyphens, and underscores. 4) Verify the constructed workspace path is within WORKSPACES_DIR using Path.resolve().

findings.title: Path Traversal in Context Builder File Operations
findings.description: forge/execution/context_builder.py reads arbitrary file paths from the codebase_map without validating that they resolve within the repository root. An attacker who can influence codebase_map content (e.g., via a malicious checkpoint or crafted repo) could inject paths like ../../etc/passwd to read arbitrary files. Two waves of security workers independently flagged this with consistent severity assessment.

locations.snippet:
abs_path = str(root / rel_path)
content = read_file_safe(abs_path)

findings.suggested_fix: Add a repo_root parameter to read_file_safe. Before reading: resolved = Path(path).resolve(); if not resolved.is_relative_to(Path(repo_root).resolve()): raise ValueError('Path traversal detected'). Apply this check in select_files_for_pass and build_codebase_inventory.

findings.title: Path Traversal in Checkpoint File Operations
findings.description: forge/execution/checkpoint.py constructs checkpoint file paths using os.path.join(repo_path, CHECKPOINT_DIR) without validating that repo_path doesn't contain traversal sequences. A malicious repo_path like /real/repo/../../etc could write checkpoint files outside the intended directory. Additionally, clear_checkpoints uses shutil.rmtree without validating the target is within expected bounds, potentially enabling symlink attacks.
findings.suggested_fix: In _checkpoint_path: resolve both repo_path and cp_dir with Path.resolve() and verify cp_dir.is_relative_to(resolved_repo). For clear_checkpoints: verify cp_dir is within expected bounds before rmtree, and check for symlinks with os.path.islink before following.

findings.title: Insecure Checkpoint Deserialization Without Integrity Verification
findings.description: Checkpoint files in .forge-checkpoints/ are loaded and deserialized without any integrity verification (no HMAC, no signature). An attacker with write access to the checkpoint directory can tamper with files to inject malicious data that gets reconstructed into CodebaseMap, AuditFinding, and other Pydantic models. While Pydantic validates types, it doesn't prevent injection of semantically malicious values (e.g., crafted file paths, finding IDs). Multiple workers flagged this consistently.

locations.snippet:
with open(path, "r") as f:
    data = json.load(f)
cp = ForgeCheckpoint(**data)

state.codebase_map = CodebaseMap(**cp.codebase_map)
state.security_findings = [AuditFinding(**f) for f in cp.security_findings]

findings.suggested_fix: Add HMAC-SHA256 signature to checkpoint files using a run-specific secret. Store signature alongside data and verify before deserializing. Alternatively, store checkpoints in a location only writable by the forge process. Also add validation of restored repo_path against current repo_path.

findings.title: God Module: forge/app.py Violates Single Responsibility
findings.description: forge/app.py is a monolithic orchestrator (~245 lines) handling: platform detection, conditional AgentField import, repo cloning, workspace management, telemetry lifecycle, checkpoint recovery, pipeline phase orchestration (discovery/triage/remediation/validation), worktree cleanup, and result construction. This was flagged by both architecture and quality workers in both waves with very high confidence. It makes the module untestable, unmaintainable, and a merge conflict hotspot.

locations.snippet: async def remediate(...) -> dict: # ~150 lines handling all pipeline phases

findings.suggested_fix: Extract into focused modules: forge/execution/repo_resolver.py (clone/path logic), forge/execution/pipeline.py (phase orchestration), forge/execution/telemetry_context.py (telemetry lifecycle wrapper). The remediate() function should delegate to these, becoming ~30 lines.

findings.title: Unhandled CalledProcessError from Git Clone Subprocess
findings.description: forge/app.py calls subprocess.run with check=True for git clone but has no try/except around it. A network failure, invalid URL, or authentication error causes an unhandled CalledProcessError to propagate up through remediate(), bypassing telemetry cleanup and worktree cleanup in the finally block (since the exception occurs before try). Two quality workers flagged this in both waves.

locations.snippet:
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "clone", "--depth=1", repo_url, workspace],
    check=True, capture_output=True, text=True,
)

findings.suggested_fix: Wrap subprocess.run in try/except subprocess.CalledProcessError and raise a user-friendly ForgeCloneError with the stderr output. Also move subprocess and re imports to module level.

findings.title: Silent Checkpoint Failures Risk Data Loss
findings.description: Both save_checkpoint and load_checkpoint catch all exceptions and log them without propagating. A checkpoint save failure during a long remediation run results in silent data loss—the user sees no error and believes progress is saved, but resume will restart from the beginning. Multiple workers flagged this in both waves.

locations.snippet:
except Exception as e:
    logger.error("Failed to save checkpoint for %s: %s", phase.value, e)

findings.suggested_fix: Add a ForgeConfig option checkpoint_failure_mode: Literal['strict', 'lenient'] = 'lenient'. In strict mode, re-raise the exception. Always log at ERROR level. For load failures, add a specific warning that a fresh run will start. For save failures in strict mode, halt the pipeline.

findings.title: File Descriptor Leak in build_codebase_inventory
findings.description: forge/execution/context_builder.py opens files with fpath.open() inside a loop without using a context manager. While CPython's reference counting typically closes files promptly, this is not guaranteed and can cause file descriptor exhaustion on large repositories or with alternative Python implementations. Two quality workers flagged this in both waves.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with: `with fpath.open(errors='replace') as f: loc = sum(1 for _ in f)`

findings.title: Duplicated File Selection Logic in context_builder.py
findings.description: select_files_for_pass and select_files_for_quality_pass in context_builder.py contain nearly identical logic for file reading, token budget management, and content assembly. Only the scoring keyword sets differ. This violates DRY and means bug fixes or improvements must be applied twice.

locations.snippet:
def select_files_for_pass(...)
def select_files_for_quality_pass(...)

findings.suggested_fix: Extract common logic into _select_files_impl(repo_path, scored_files, token_budget) -> str. Both public functions score files differently then call the shared impl.

findings.title: Telemetry Context Manager Misuse — Manual __enter__/__exit__ Calls
findings.description: forge/app.py manually calls _telemetry_ctx.__enter__() and later _telemetry_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None) instead of using async with or contextlib. The None arguments to __exit__ don't propagate exception information correctly. If an exception occurs before the try block but after __enter__, cleanup is skipped. Two quality workers flagged this in both waves.

locations.snippet:
_telemetry_ctx = telemetry.activate()
_telemetry_ctx.__enter__()

if _telemetry_ctx is not None:
    _telemetry_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)

findings.suggested_fix: Refactor remediate() to use `async with telemetry.activate():` if the context manager supports it, or use contextlib.AsyncExitStack to manage multiple context managers. This is part of the broader app.py refactor (F-005).

findings.title: Unvalidated FORGE_PORT Environment Variable Causes Crash
findings.description: forge/__main__.py calls int(os.getenv('FORGE_PORT', '8004')) without try/except. A misconfigured environment (e.g., FORGE_PORT=disabled) raises an unhandled ValueError at startup. Flagged by both security and quality workers.

locations.snippet: port = int(os.getenv("FORGE_PORT", "8004"))

findings.title: Missing JSON Error Handling in CLI Report Command
findings.description: forge/cli.py reads and parses a report JSON file with json.loads() without catching JSONDecodeError. A corrupted or partially written report file causes an unhandled crash instead of a user-friendly error message.

locations.snippet: data = json.loads(latest.read_text())

findings.suggested_fix: Wrap in try/except json.JSONDecodeError and emit a user-friendly error via typer.echo.

findings.title: Conditional Import Pattern Creates Fragile Platform Detection
findings.description: forge/app.py uses try/except ImportError to conditionally import AgentField and sets app=None if unavailable. This implicit mode switching makes it hard to reason about which features are active, and function-level imports scattered through remediate() further obscure dependencies. Flagged by architecture workers in both waves.
findings.suggested_fix: Create an explicit PlatformMode enum. Create separate entry modules forge/platform_app.py and forge/standalone.py. Move function-level imports to module level. The mode should be determined once at startup and injected consistently.

findings.title: Circular Import Risk via Function-Level Lazy Imports
findings.description: forge/execution/checkpoint.py imports forge.schemas inside restore_state() at function call time. This hides a potential circular dependency—if schemas ever imports from checkpoint (directly or transitively), the code breaks at runtime. ARCH-004 and ARCH-009 both flagged this pattern across modules.
findings.suggested_fix: Move imports to module top-level. Use TYPE_CHECKING guard for type-only annotations to break any actual circular dependency: `if TYPE_CHECKING: from forge.schemas import ForgeExecutionState`

findings.title: Missing Type Annotation on restore_state Return Value
findings.description: forge/execution/checkpoint.py declares restore_state() -> Any despite always returning ForgeExecutionState. This loses static type safety for all callers and makes the API contract unclear.
findings.suggested_fix: Change return type to ForgeExecutionState (using TYPE_CHECKING import if needed to avoid circular imports).

findings.title: Configuration Scattered Across Multiple Modules
findings.description: Magic numbers and configuration values are defined in multiple places: CHARS_PER_TOKEN=4 and DEFAULT_TOKEN_BUDGET=80_000 in context_builder.py, WORKSPACES_DIR in app.py, max retries hardcoded in forge_executor.py. There is no single authoritative configuration surface. Flagged by multiple architecture workers.

locations.snippet:
CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4
DEFAULT_TOKEN_BUDGET = 80_000
WORKSPACES_DIR = os.getenv("WORKSPACES_DIR", "/workspaces")

findings.suggested_fix: Add token_budget, chars_per_token, workspaces_dir, max_inner_retries fields to ForgeConfig in config.py. Reference ForgeConfig in all modules that currently have magic numbers.

findings.title: Inconsistent Error Handling in asyncio.gather Calls
findings.description: forge/execution/forge_executor.py uses asyncio.gather with return_exceptions=True and substitutes default empty results for agent failures. This means a test generator or code reviewer failure silently produces an empty/default result rather than clearly failing the fix attempt. The behavior is intentional but undocumented and potentially masks real failures.
findings.suggested_fix: Document explicitly why silent default results are acceptable (or not). Add a metric counter for agent failures. Consider adding a max_agent_failures threshold in ForgeConfig that triggers a fix failure rather than silent default.

findings.title: Checkpoint Resume Validation Missing Repo Path Check
findings.description: forge/app.py resumes from checkpoint based only on forge_run_id without validating that the checkpoint's repo_path matches the current run's repo_path. Running FORGE on repo B after a failed run on repo A in the same workspace could result in applying repo A's state to repo B.
findings.suggested_fix: Add validation: if cp.repo_path != resolved_repo_path: logger.warning('Checkpoint repo_path mismatch, ignoring checkpoint'); cp = None. Also validate forge_run_id format.

findings.title: Hardcoded Role Strings Duplicated Across Config Dicts
findings.description: Role name strings like 'codebase_analyst', 'security_auditor', etc. appear in FORGE_ROLE_TO_MODEL_FIELD, FORGE_DEFAULT_MODELS, and ROLE_TO_PROVIDER dictionaries in config.py, plus referenced in other files. A role rename requires updating multiple locations.

locations.snippet:
FORGE_ROLE_TO_MODEL_FIELD: dict[str, str] = {"codebase_analyst": ..., ...}
ROLE_TO_PROVIDER: dict[str, str] = {"codebase_analyst": ..., ...}

findings.suggested_fix: Define an AgentRole enum (or StrEnum in Python 3.11+) with all role names. Use it as keys in all dicts. This provides IDE support and prevents typos.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting on LLM API Calls
findings.description: The FORGE system invokes multiple LLM agents concurrently (enabled by enable_parallel_audit=True) without any rate limiting, backoff, or circuit breaker. This can cause API quota exhaustion, unexpected cost spikes, or provider-side throttling that manifests as opaque errors. Flagged by both security workers in both waves.

locations.snippet: enable_parallel_audit: bool = True
async def run_inner_loop(...)

findings.suggested_fix: Add max_concurrent_invocations and max_requests_per_minute to ForgeConfig. Implement a semaphore-based concurrency limiter in forge_executor.py. Add exponential backoff for rate limit (429) responses.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Potentially Exposed in Logs and Telemetry
findings.description: The telemetry system logs full finding descriptions, summaries, and file changes (which may contain extracted secrets or sensitive code) via log_training_pair. Additionally, AGENTFIELD_API_KEY is passed to the Agent constructor and could be captured by debug loggers. Flagged by security workers in both waves.

locations.snippet: api_key=os.getenv("AGENTFIELD_API_KEY")
telemetry.log_training_pair(..., description=finding.description, ...)

findings.suggested_fix: 1) Add a logging.Filter that redacts values matching API key patterns. 2) Add a sanitize_for_telemetry() function that strips potential secrets from finding descriptions before logging. 3) Document that telemetry files should not be committed.

findings.title: sys.modules Manipulation in Integration Test Conftest is Fragile
findings.description: tests/integration/conftest.py directly manipulates sys.modules to inject a mock agentfield module. This is a global side effect that couples test execution order to import order, can cause intermittent failures, and makes it impossible to run individual integration tests in isolation. Flagged by both architecture and quality workers in both waves.

locations.snippet: sys.modules.setdefault("agentfield", _mock_agentfield)

findings.suggested_fix: Use pytest's monkeypatch fixture scoped to session, or use unittest.mock.patch as a decorator on tests that need the mock. If module-level mocking is unavoidable (due to import-time side effects), document clearly and add a comment explaining why.

findings.title: Parallel Test File Writes to Shared Benchmark Log Without Locking
findings.description: tests/integration/conftest.py appends to .forge-benchmarks/cost_log.jsonl from multiple test processes without file locking. Parallel test runs (e.g., pytest-xdist) can corrupt this file.

locations.snippet: with open(_BENCHMARK_LOG, "a") as f:

findings.suggested_fix: Use fcntl.flock for POSIX or a threading.Lock for single-process parallelism. Alternatively, write per-worker files (e.g., cost_log_worker{id}.jsonl) and merge in a final step.

findings.title: Test Helper Functions Duplicated Across Test Files
findings.description: _copy_golden in test_golden_suite.py and _copy_golden_codebase in test_hive_live_e2e.py serve the same purpose with slightly different signatures. Mock response builders (_coder_ok, _test_ok, _review_ok) could leverage conftest factories. DRY violation increases maintenance burden.

locations.snippet: def _copy_golden(name: str, tmp_path) -> str:
def _copy_golden_codebase(name: str, dest: Path) -> Path:

findings.suggested_fix: Consolidate into a single copy_golden(name, dest_dir) function in tests/conftest.py or tests/fixtures/helpers.py. Add assertion that source directory exists before copying.

findings.title: Hardcoded /tmp Paths in Test State Helpers
findings.description: tests/integration/test_execute_remediation.py hardcodes /tmp/test-repo and /tmp/test-artifacts as paths in ForgeExecutionState. These can conflict between parallel test runs and may not be writable on all systems.

locations.snippet: state = ForgeExecutionState(repo_path="/tmp/test-repo")

findings.suggested_fix: Convert _state_with_plan() to a @pytest.fixture that uses the tmp_path fixture for isolated, system-appropriate temp directories.

findings.title: Fragile String-Based Reasoner Dispatch in Tests
findings.description: tests/integration/test_execute_remediation.py uses substring matching ('run_coder' in reasoner) to route mock responses. If production reasoner names change, tests silently return empty dicts rather than failing loudly.

locations.snippet:
if "run_coder" in reasoner:
    return _coder_ok(fid)

findings.suggested_fix: Import reasoner name constants from production code (or a shared constants module) rather than using magic strings. Add a final else branch that raises ValueError for unrecognized reasoners.

findings.title: Golden Codebases Contain Real Vulnerabilities — Risk of Misuse
findings.description: tests/golden/codebases/ contains SQL injection, hardcoded secrets, and missing auth — intentionally for testing but without clear documentation. These could be accidentally packaged into distributions or used as templates. Multiple workers flagged this (as info/low in tests context).

locations.snippet: const API_KEY = "sk-live-12345abcdef67890ghijklmnop";

@app.get("/admin/users")
def admin_list_users(): # No authentication check!

findings.suggested_fix: 1) Add a README.md in tests/golden/codebases/ explaining these are intentionally vulnerable test fixtures. 2) Add a .gitignore entry or setup.cfg exclude to prevent packaging. 3) Add a top-of-file comment in each file: '# INTENTIONALLY INSECURE - test fixture only'.

findings.title: Inconsistent Async Test Marker Usage
findings.description: Some async tests explicitly use @pytest.mark.asyncio while others rely on auto-detection. This can cause tests to be silently skipped in strict mode configurations.

locations.snippet: @pytest.mark.asyncio

findings.suggested_fix: Set asyncio_mode = 'auto' in pytest.ini or pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options] to normalize behavior, then remove redundant explicit markers.

findings.title: resolved_models() Dict Created on Every Call — Performance
findings.description: forge/config.py ForgeConfig.resolved_models() creates a new dictionary on every call by copying FORGE_DEFAULT_MODELS and applying overrides. model_for_role() calls resolved_models() internally. This is called in tight executor loops.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache the result using @functools.cached_property or a private _resolved_models field initialized in model_post_init().

findings.title: Test conftest.py Combines Too Many Responsibilities
findings.description: tests/conftest.py (~200 lines) combines schema factories, pytest hooks (pytest_addoption, pytest_configure, pytest_collection_modifyitems), and fixtures. This makes it hard to navigate and maintain.
findings.suggested_fix: Split into: tests/conftest.py (fixtures only), tests/pytest_plugins.py (hooks), tests/fixtures/factories.py (factory functions). Keep tests/fixtures/schemas.py as re-export.

findings.title: Command Injection via Git Clone with Unsanitized repo_url
findings.description: In `forge/app.py`, the `_resolve_repo_path` function directly uses the `repo_url` parameter in a `subprocess.run` call without any validation or sanitization. An attacker could provide a malicious URL containing shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary commands on the system.

locations.snippet:
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "clone", "--depth=1", repo_url, workspace],
    check=True, capture_output=True, text=True,
)

findings.suggested_fix: Implement strict URL validation using a whitelist of allowed protocols (only 'https://' and 'ssh://' with known host patterns), validate the URL format with a regex, and use `shlex.quote()` to escape any shell metacharacters in the URL. Consider using a URL parser to extract and validate the hostname before passing to subprocess.

findings.title: Path Traversal Vulnerability in File Context Selection
findings.description: The `context_builder.py` file reading functions do not validate or sanitize file paths before reading. An attacker who can control the codebase_map could inject paths with `../` sequences to read sensitive files outside the repository (e.g., `../../etc/passwd`, `../../.env`).

locations.snippet:
for score, rel_path in scored_files:
    ...
    abs_path = str(root / rel_path)
    content = read_file_safe(abs_path)

findings.suggested_fix: Add path traversal validation in `read_file_safe` and before constructing paths. Use `Path.resolve()` to resolve the absolute path and verify it starts with the repository root using `resolved_path.is_relative_to(repo_root)` or equivalent check.

findings.title: Insecure Deserialization in Checkpoint Loading
findings.description: The checkpoint system in `checkpoint.py` loads JSON files without integrity verification and reconstructs complex objects (including potential code execution via Pydantic models). An attacker with write access to `.forge-checkpoints/` could tamper with checkpoint files to inject malicious data or cause denial of service.

locations.snippet:
def restore_state(
    cp: ForgeCheckpoint,
) -> Any:
    ...
    state = ForgeExecutionState(
        forge_run_id=cp.forge_run_id,
        mode=ForgeMode.FULL,
        repo_path=cp.repo_path,
        artifacts_dir=cp.artifacts_dir,
    )

    # Restore discovery outputs
    if cp.codebase_map:
        state.codebase_map = CodebaseMap(**cp.codebase_map)
    state.security_findings = [AuditFinding(**f) for f in cp.security_findings]

findings.suggested_fix: Add HMAC signature verification to checkpoint files using a secret key stored securely. Verify the signature before deserializing. Alternatively, add schema validation using Pydantic's strict mode and add type coercion restrictions.

findings.title: Missing Input Validation on Environment-Derived Configuration
findings.description: Multiple functions accept configuration via environment variables without validation. The `main()` function in `__main__.py` converts `FORGE_PORT` to int without try/except, allowing DoS via malformed values. Similarly, `app` initialization uses unchecked environment variables.

locations.snippet:
port = int(os.getenv("FORGE_PORT", "8004"))
host = os.getenv("FORGE_HOST", "0.0.0.0")

NODE_ID = os.getenv("FORGE_NODE_ID", "forge-engine")
WORKSPACES_DIR = os.getenv("WORKSPACES_DIR", "/workspaces")

findings.suggested_fix: Add validation for all environment variables: port should be validated as positive integer in valid range (1-65535), host should be validated as valid IP or hostname, NODE_ID should be validated against allowed characters pattern.

findings.title: Potential Arbitrary File Write via Worktree Operations
findings.description: The code uses git worktrees for isolation during fixes. If `worktree_path` is derived from user input without proper validation, an attacker could create worktrees in arbitrary locations. The `_resolve_repo_path` function creates directories based on repo names extracted from URLs.

locations.snippet:
workspace = os.path.join(WORKSPACES_DIR, name)

        if Path(workspace).is_dir():
            logger.info("Reusing existing workspace: %s", workspace)
            return workspace

        # Clone
        logger.info("Cloning %s → %s", repo_url, workspace)
        os.makedirs(workspace, exist_ok=True)
        import subprocess
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "clone", "--depth=1", repo_url, workspace],
            check=True, capture_output=True, text=True,
        )

findings.suggested_fix: Validate the derived workspace path is within an expected parent directory (e.g., verify `os.path.abspath(workspace).startswith(WORKSPACES_DIR)`). Use a allowlist of permitted characters for the extracted repo name.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting on API Endpoints or Agent Invocations
findings.description: The FORGE system makes multiple LLM API calls but has no built-in rate limiting. The configuration allows high concurrency (`enable_parallel_audit`) without throttling. This could lead to API quota exhaustion or cost spikes.

locations.snippet:
enable_parallel_audit: bool = True  # Run audit passes concurrently
    enable_learning: bool = True  # Log training data for fine-tuning flywheel

findings.suggested_fix: Implement rate limiting using a token bucket or sliding window algorithm. Add configuration options for max requests per minute and max concurrent invocations. Consider adding a circuit breaker pattern for external API calls.

findings.title: Insufficient Input Validation in Config Resolution
findings.description: The `ForgeConfig` class uses Pydantic but allows arbitrary dictionaries via the `models` field. While `extra="forbid"` is set, there's no validation that model names map to valid roles or that the dict values are legitimate model identifiers. Malformed config could cause unexpected behavior.

locations.snippet:
class ForgeConfig(BaseModel):
    """Configuration for a FORGE run.

    Mirrors SWE-AF's BuildConfig pattern with FORGE-specific defaults.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    runtime: Literal["open_code"] = "open_code"
    models: dict[str, str] | None = None  # role -> model overrides

findings.suggested_fix: Add a validator that checks the `models` dictionary keys are valid roles from `FORGE_ROLE_TO_MODEL_FIELD` and values match expected model ID patterns (e.g., `provider/model-name` format).

findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposure in Logging
findings.description: The code logs various data including potential API keys, repo paths, and finding details. While `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is set in environment after validation, the `AGENTFIELD_API_KEY` is passed directly to the Agent constructor and could be logged inadvertently.

locations.snippet:
NODE_ID = os.getenv("FORGE_NODE_ID", "forge-engine")
WORKSPACES_DIR = os.getenv("WORKSPACES_DIR", "/workspaces")

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

if Agent is not None:
    app = Agent(
        node_id=NODE_ID,
        version="0.1.0",
        description="FORGE: Framework for Orchestrated Remediation & Governance Engine",
        agentfield_server=os.getenv("AGENTFIELD_SERVER", "http://localhost:8080"),
        api_key=os.getenv("AGENTFIELD_API_KEY"),
    )

findings.suggested_fix: Ensure API keys are redacted in logs by using a custom log filter or by explicitly avoiding logging any configuration containing secrets. Use `logging.Filter` to mask sensitive environment variables.

findings.title: Missing Authentication/Authorization for CLI Commands
findings.description: The CLI (`cli.py`) has no authentication mechanism. While API key is required for LLM calls, there's no access control on who can run scans or fixes against local repositories. In multi-user environments, this could be exploited.

locations.snippet:
def _check_api_key(api_key: str | None) -> str:
    """Resolve the OpenRouter API key from flag or environment."""
    key = api_key or os.getenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY")
    if not key:
        typer.echo(
            "Error: OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not set.\n"
            "Set it in your environment or pass --api-key:\n\n"
            "  export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-v1-...\n"
            "  vibe2prod scan ./my-app\n",
            err=True,
        )
        raise typer.Exit(1)
    os.environ["OPENROUTER_API_KEY"] = key
    return key

findings.suggested_fix: For multi-user environments, consider adding authentication (e.g., API key validation stored securely) or OS-level permissions. Document that this tool should only be used in trusted environments.

findings.title: Potential DoS via Token Budget Exhaustion in Context Building
findings.description: The `select_files_for_pass` function uses a token budget but doesn't validate input parameters. Large `token_budget` values or many files could cause memory exhaustion. The `_estimate_tokens` function uses a rough approximation that could be significantly off for certain content types.
findings.suggested_fix: Add bounds checking on `token_budget` parameter (e.g., max 150000 tokens). Add timeout for file reading operations. Consider streaming file processing for very large repositories.

findings.title: God Module: forge/app.py Contains Too Many Responsibilities
findings.description: forge/app.py acts as a monolithic orchestrator handling platform detection, repo cloning, telemetry activation, checkpoint recovery, pipeline execution (discovery/triage/remediation/validation), worktree management, and result construction. This violates the Single Responsibility Principle and makes the module difficult to test, maintain, and extend. Changes to any part of the pipeline require modifying this central file.

locations.snippet: Contains platform detection, repo cloning, telemetry, checkpoint recovery, and all 4 pipeline phases in single module

findings.suggested_fix: Extract responsibilities into separate modules: 1) RepoResolver for clone/path resolution, 2) PipelineOrchestrator for phase sequencing, 3) TelemetryManager for telemetry lifecycle, 4) WorktreeManager for git operations. Use a pipeline definition class to configure phase order.

findings.title: Layering Violation: CLI Directly Couples to Execution Engine
findings.description: forge/cli.py directly imports and calls run_standalone from forge.standalone, mixing presentation logic with execution logic. The CLI should interact through a well-defined API or service layer, not directly invoke internal execution functions. This creates tight coupling that prevents swapping the execution engine.

locations.snippet: from forge.standalone import run_standalone

findings.suggested_fix: Create a public API module (e.g., forge/api.py) with functions like scan_repository() and fix_repository() that the CLI imports. This provides a stable contract between presentation and execution layers.

findings.title: Conditional Import Creates Fragile Architecture
findings.description: forge/app.py uses 'try/except ImportError' to conditionally create the AgentField app or set app=None. This pattern makes the platform/standalone mode distinction implicit and error-prone. The codebase cannot clearly express which features require AgentField vs standalone mode.
findings.suggested_fix: Use an explicit mode configuration enum (PlatformMode.STANDALONE vs PlatformMode.AGENTFIELD) passed at startup. Create separate entry points (forge/platform.py and forge/standalone.py) that each configure the appropriate app instance.

findings.title: Circular Import Risk with Lazy Schema Imports
findings.description: forge/execution/checkpoint.py imports forge.schemas inside the restore_state() function rather than at module level. This creates a hidden circular import dependency - if schemas ever imports from checkpoint, the code will break. It also makes the module's dependencies unclear at static analysis time.
findings.suggested_fix: Move imports to the top of the module. Use TYPE_CHECKING block for type-only imports if needed. Add explicit dependencies in a requirements or package manifest.

findings.title: Configuration Scattered Across Multiple Locations
findings.description: Configuration is defined in multiple places: FORGE_DEFAULT_MODELS in config.py, hardcoded values in context_builder.py (DEFAULT_TOKEN_BUDGET=80_000, CHARS_PER_TOKEN=4), magic numbers in forge_executor.py (max retries), and worktree paths in app.py. There's no unified configuration object, making it difficult to override settings or understand the full configuration surface.

locations.snippet:
CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 4
DEFAULT_TOKEN_BUDGET = 80_000
WORKSPACES_DIR = os.getenv("WORKSPACES_DIR", "/workspaces")

findings.suggested_fix: Consolidate all configuration into ForgeConfig in config.py. Add token_budget, chars_per_token, workspaces_dir, and other settings. Use environment variable overrides consistently through ForgeConfig.

findings.title: Telemetry Activation Coupled to Business Logic
findings.description: In forge/app.py:remediate(), telemetry is activated inline within the function using context manager patterns. This couples telemetry (a cross-cutting concern) directly to the main execution path, making it difficult to disable or replace telemetry implementation without modifying core logic.

locations.snippet:
telemetry = ForgeTelemetry(run_id=state.forge_run_id)
_telemetry_ctx = telemetry.activate()
_telemetry_ctx.__enter__()

findings.suggested_fix: Extract telemetry initialization into a middleware or context manager that wraps the entire pipeline. Consider using a decorator pattern to separate telemetry concerns from the remediate() function.

findings.title: Inconsistent Error Handling in Checkpoint System
findings.description: forge/execution/checkpoint.py silently catches and logs exceptions without re-raising (lines 70-73, 101-104). This masks failures that may be critical for crash recovery. A checkpoint save failure could lead to lost work without the user being aware.

locations.snippet:
except Exception as e:
    logger.error("Failed to save checkpoint for %s: %s", phase.value, e)

findings.suggested_fix: Add a configuration option for checkpoint failure behavior: strict (raise exception), lenient (log and continue), or advisory (log warning). In critical pipelines, default to strict mode.

findings.title: Missing Abstractions in Context Builder
findings.description: forge/execution/context_builder.py mixes file selection logic (keyword matching, scoring) with file reading and token budgeting in the same functions. These are separate concerns that should be abstracted: FileSelector, ContentReader, and TokenBudgetAllocator classes would improve testability and reusability.

Additionally, the workspace path derived from the URL is used directly without sanitization.

locations.snippet:
def _resolve_repo_path(repo_url: str, repo_path: str) -> str:
    """Determine the repo path — clone if needed, else use provided."""
    if repo_path and Path(repo_path).is_dir():
        return repo_path

    if repo_url:
        # Derive workspace path from URL
        import re
        match = re.search(r"/([^/]+?)(?:\.git)?$", repo_url.rstrip("/"))
        name = match.group(1) if match else "repo"
        workspace = os.path.join(WORKSPACES_DIR, name)

        if Path(workspace).is_dir():
            logger.info("Reusing existing workspace: %s", workspace)
            return workspace

        # Clone
        logger.info("Cloning %s → %s", repo_url, workspace)
        os.makedirs(workspace, exist_ok=True)
        import subprocess
        subprocess.run(
            ["git", "clone", "--depth=1", repo_url, workspace],
            check=True, capture_output=True, text=True,
        )

findings.suggested_fix: Validate repo_url is a valid HTTPS URL before cloning. Add URL scheme validation to ensure only https:// URLs are allowed (not file:// or git://). Use urlparse to validate the URL format and restrict to trusted domains if possible.

def restore_state(
    cp: ForgeCheckpoint,
) -> Any:
    """Restore ForgeExecutionState from a checkpoint.

    Returns a populated ForgeExecutionState ready to resume.
    """
    from forge.schemas import (
        AuditFinding,
        CodebaseMap,
        CoderFixResult,
        ForgeExecutionState,
        ForgeMode,
        IntegrationValidationResult,
        ProductionReadinessReport,
        RemediationPlan,
        TriageResult,
    )

    state = ForgeExecutionState(
        forge_run_id=cp.forge_run_id,
        mode=ForgeMode.FULL,
        repo_path=cp.repo_path,
        artifacts_dir=cp.artifacts_dir,
    )

    # Restore discovery outputs
    if cp.codebase_map:
        state.codebase_map = CodebaseMap(**cp.codebase_map)
    state.security_findings = [AuditFinding(**f) for f in cp.security_findings]

findings.suggested_fix: Add validation of checkpoint integrity. Consider adding a checksum/signature to checkpoints that can be verified before restoration. Also validate the restored repo_path exists and is a valid directory before using it.

findings.title: Hardcoded Secrets in Source Code

findings.title: SQL Injection Vulnerability
findings.description: User-supplied input is directly concatenated into SQL queries without parameterization or sanitization, allowing attackers to manipulate query logic and potentially access unauthorized data.
findings.suggested_fix: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) with placeholders (e.g., $1, $2) instead of string interpolation. Example: pool.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = $1', [name])

findings.title: Missing Authentication on Admin Endpoints
findings.description: Admin endpoints (/admin/users, /admin/users/{user_id}) have no authentication or authorization checks, allowing any unauthenticated user to access sensitive administrative functionality.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement authentication (e.g., JWT tokens, session-based auth) and role-based authorization (RBAC) to verify that only authorized users can access admin endpoints. Use dependency injection patterns (e.g., FastAPI's Depends) to enforce access control.

findings.title: Information Disclosure via Stack Traces
findings.description: Error handlers expose full stack traces in HTTP responses, revealing internal application details, file paths, and library versions that could assist attackers in identifying vulnerabilities.

locations.snippet: res.status(500).json({ error: err.message, stack: err.stack });

findings.suggested_fix: Disable debug mode in production. Configure error handlers to return generic error messages to clients while logging detailed errors server-side. Example: res.status(500).json({ error: 'Internal server error' }) and log full details to a secure logging system.

findings.title: Missing Input Validation
findings.description: User input from request bodies is used directly without validation or sanitization, potentially allowing injection attacks, malformed data storage, or application crashes.

locations.snippet:
const { name, email, password } = req.body;
// No input validation

findings.suggested_fix: Implement input validation using schema validation libraries (e.g., Pydantic for Python, Joi for Node.js, Zod for TypeScript). Validate data types, required fields, format constraints (email, length), and sanitize special characters.

findings.title: Missing Security Headers and Rate Limiting
findings.description: The Express application lacks rate limiting, CORS configuration, and security headers (Helmet), exposing the application to brute-force attacks, cross-site scripting via CORS, and various client-side attacks.
findings.suggested_fix: Add rate limiting using express-rate-limit, configure CORS with appropriate origin restrictions, and use Helmet.js to set security headers (Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, etc.).

findings.title: Insecure Session Cookie Configuration
findings.description: Flask session cookies are not configured with security flags (SECURE, HTTPONLY, SAME SITE), making them vulnerable to XSS theft and CSRF attacks.

# app.config["SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY"] = False (default)

findings.suggested_fix: Configure secure session cookies: app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE'] = True, app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY'] = True, app.config['SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE'] = 'Lax'

findings.title: Sensitive Data Exposure via Console Logging
findings.description: Authentication tokens and API keys are logged to the browser console, potentially exposing sensitive credentials to anyone with browser access or through browser extensions.

findings.title: Hardcoded Database Connection URL

findings.title: Missing Error Handling in Fetch Calls
findings.description: React components make API calls without error handling, which can lead to unhandled promise rejections and poor user experience. While not a direct security vulnerability, it can expose application state issues.
findings.suggested_fix: Add .catch() handlers to all fetch calls and implement proper error states in the UI. Example: fetch(url).then(res => { if (!res.ok) throw new Error(...); return res.json(); }).catch(err => { ... })

findings.title: Circular Import Dependency
findings.description: Python files have circular imports (main.py imports from utils.py, utils.py imports from main.py) which can cause runtime import errors and unpredictable module initialization.

from main import Product  # Circular import!

findings.suggested_fix: Refactor to eliminate circular dependencies by moving shared code to a separate module or using lazy imports within functions rather than module-level imports.

findings.title: Global sys.modules manipulation in test infrastructure
findings.description: tests/integration/conftest.py directly manipulates sys.modules to mock the agentfield module before any imports. This creates tight coupling between test infrastructure and production module structure, makes tests fragile to module reorganization, and bypasses normal import mechanisms.

locations.snippet: sys.modules.setdefault("agentfield", _mock_agentfield)

findings.suggested_fix: Use a pytest plugin or conftest at the root level with proper autouse fixtures that mock at the call site rather than module load time. Consider using unittest.mock.patch at the import point (e.g., patch('forge.execution.forge_executor.Agent')) rather than modifying sys.modules directly.

findings.title: String-based reasoner dispatch coupling
findings.description: Integration tests use magic strings like 'run_coder', 'run_test_generator', 'run_code_reviewer' to determine which mock response to return. This creates brittle coupling where test behavior depends on exact string matching with implementation reasoner names.

locations.snippet: if "run_coder" in reasoner:

findings.suggested_fix: Define an enum or constant class for reasoner names that can be imported by both production code and tests. Use constants instead of magic strings, or consider a more robust dispatch mechanism like passing mock responses keyed by finding_id.

findings.title: Parallel test execution side effects - benchmark file writes
findings.description: The forge_telemetry fixture in tests/integration/conftest.py writes to a shared file (.forge-benchmarks/cost_log.jsonl) without any locking mechanism. When tests run in parallel, this can cause file corruption or lost benchmark entries.

locations.snippet: with open(_BENCHMARK_LOG, "a") as f:

findings.suggested_fix: Use thread-safe file writing (e.g., file locking with fcntl, or writing to separate per-worker files that are merged afterward), or disable this feature when running tests in parallel mode.

findings.title: Module-level patching of imports
findings.description: Tests patch specific module paths like 'forge.execution.worktree.create_worktree' rather than testing against abstractions. This couples tests to implementation file structure and makes refactoring difficult.

locations.snippet: @patch("forge.execution.worktree.create_worktree", return_value="/tmp/test-worktree")

findings.title: Inconsistent test factory patterns
findings.description: tests/conftest.py mixes pytest fixtures (forge_config, mock_app) with standalone factory functions (make_finding, make_codebase_map). This inconsistency makes it unclear which pattern to use and can lead to tests that don't use shared fixtures.

findings.description: The golden codebases (e.g., fastapi_monolith) contain intentional circular imports and god modules that tests rely on. While this is intentional for testing detection capabilities, it creates implicit dependencies on bad patterns that could mislead developers.

findings.title: Golden Codebases Contain Real Security Vulnerabilities

findings.title: Duplicate Factory Pattern in conftest.py

findings.title: Inconsistent Fixture Usage Patterns

findings.description: The skip_unless_live fixture checks for environment variables after already determining tests should run, but doesn't handle KeyError if config.getoption fails in unexpected ways.

findings.title: Golden Test File Copy Without Verification
findings.description: The _copy_golden function in test_golden_suite.py copies directories without verifying the source exists, which could cause confusing errors.

findings.title: Path Traversal in Golden Codebase Copy Function
findings.description: The _copy_golden_codebase function in test_hive_live_e2e.py accepts a 'name' parameter directly from test parameters and uses it to construct paths without validation. An attacker who controls the test parameter could use path traversal sequences (e.g., '../../../etc') to write files outside the intended tmp_path directory. While tests are typically not exposed to untrusted input, this creates a vulnerability chain with the neighbor finding about arbitrary file write via worktree operations.
findings.suggested_fix: Add validation to ensure the name parameter doesn't contain path traversal sequences. Use os.path.normpath() and verify the resolved path is within the dest directory: `resolved = (dest / name).resolve(); if not str(resolved).startswith(str(dest.resolve())): raise ValueError('Path traversal detected')`

findings.title: Similar Path Traversal in Golden Test Suite
findings.description: The _copy_golden function in test_golden_suite.py has the same path traversal vulnerability pattern. While the 'name' parameter comes from hardcoded test parameters (@pytest.mark.parametrize), the pattern is inconsistent with secure coding practices.

    dst = str(tmp_path / name)

findings.suggested_fix: Normalize and validate the path to ensure it stays within tmp_path: `normalized = os.path.normpath(name); if '..' in normalized.split(os.sep): raise ValueError('Invalid path')`

findings.title: Mock Module Substitution at Sys Module Level

findings.title: Hardcoded Test Credentials in Golden Codebases

subprocess.run(["git", "init"], cwd=repo, check=True, capture_output=True)
